---
title: Findings reference admission
description: Refuse citations that the accepted model request did not serve, without using another model.
---

`.findings()` checks the identity of each library-owned
`_findings.previous[].toolCallId` before invoking a proposed tool and before
accepting a JSON answer. This is a deterministic structural check. An admitted
ID does **not** prove the model's assertions or the source's conclusions.

<CodeFile

  region="reference-admission"

See the mock-only [runnable example](https://github.com/footprintjs/agentfootprint/blob/main/examples/features/104-findings-reference-admission.ts).

## What changed

Previously, the schema offered IDs as guidance and the ledger preserved unknown
IDs, but the dispatch door could still invoke a tool carrying an unknown
citation. Such proposals are now refused before argument-ask context,
permission checks, credentials, before-tool middleware or `tool.execute`.
An independent valid call in the same batch keeps its normal dispatch or ask.

The check uses the request that produced the **accepted response**, after the
library's retry/fallback boundary and any reported replay preparation. It does
not borrow a failed attempt's request, a future sibling's result, another run,
a receipt hash or an ID that exists only in broad history. Custom providers
and wrappers must forward the library's hooks and accurately report their
own replay preparation; the library cannot inspect an unreported private wire
rewrite inside a custom provider.

## Identity, execution and visibility

Body visibility describes the recorded text actually sent, not the contents of
an artifact behind it. Equal source bytes remain body data even when their JSON
resembles a ticket; admission does not import authority or refs from that shape.

- A unique executed result actually served to that response can be referenced.
  The schema's advisory offer cap and retirement rules stay unchanged: a
  uniquely served older ID outside the enum is still identifiable.
- A ticket can identify an executed result while withholding its body. Identity
  admission does not treat that body as visible or validate an assertion about it.
  Other request rewrites have unknown body visibility unless their carrier is a known ticket.
- A batch-settlement notice can have a known identity while explicitly saying
  its call was **not dispatched**. It cannot authorize executed-result evidence.
- Duplicate occurrences of an ID are ambiguous, even if their bodies match.
- Missing or oversized capture is unknown, never promoted to complete evidence.
  Capture is bounded to 4,096 distinct result IDs per message list and 65,536
  ID characters across the original and sent lists; crossing either limit
  refuses references rather than silently dropping evidence.

Malformed attempted reserved metadata is refused too; it cannot erase its own
citation by failing the lenient declaration parser. A ToolProvider tool whose
author owns `_findings` retains that argument as application data under the
existing ownership rule.

## Refusal and correction

A refused tool proposal receives a fixed teaching result. Its declared unknown
standing and assertions stay on the findings ledger; a bounded
`reference-refusal` diagnostic is stored beside them. These rows are diagnostic
and model-declared evidence, not proof that a foreign ID exists or that an
assertion is true. Malformed attempted frames are capped at 8,192 characters
and explicitly marked when truncated. Conversation redaction covers the new
request witness and the ledger through the existing conversation vocabulary.

An invalid final JSON answer raises `MessageDeniedError`. If an output schema
already configured retries, only that existing allowance and the remaining
iteration budget can be spent correcting it. Plain findings adds no corrective
model call or separate budget. Output middleware cannot erase an invalid raw
citation to make it pass; middleware-introduced invalid citations are checked
again before final settlement.

Streaming tokens are drafts. Tokens already emitted before final parsing remain
visible to the subscriber; final admission cannot retract them. Phase A does
not buffer streams or claim that draft text was never shown.

## Continued and paused runs

A new model request that re-serves old history creates its own fresh witness;
older saved records need no historical admission receipt for that new request.
Resuming an already proposed paused call instead needs its original proposal
and request witness. Missing evidence refuses that proposal before remaining
callbacks; expanded future history cannot manufacture a grant. Refusal rows
survive checkpoints and remain diagnostics on continuation or error resume.

`recordReceipt: false` disables optional receipts, not live admission. A
checkpoint or witness is trusted host state; this is not a signature or a
sandbox against a host deliberately altering its own run.

## Scope

This phase leaves schema enums, tool and system layouts, instruction cache
policies, `toolsVaryPerCall`, cache markers and normal request rendering as they
were. Agents without findings do not capture the request witness or add producer markers.
A shared entry-boundary correction also applies without findings: if dispatch
context or time preparation fails before `execute` is entered, resumed calls no
longer report entry or run after-tool middleware. The nominal reference and wire
identity checks do not promise identity for that previously misclassified failure.

It uses no model, network lookup or paid validation service. Cache layout work
and any paid benchmark are separate work; no savings or hosted behavior has
been measured by this feature's mock tests.
